newsitem.title: USA: McDougal sentenced to 3 years in Whitewater case.
newsitem.headline: McDougal sentenced to 3 years in Whitewater case.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's former business partner James McDougal was sentenced on Monday to three years in prison and three years probation for fraud and conspiracy charges linked to the Whitewater investigation.

The sentence handed out by U.S. District Judge George Howard was far below the maximum 81 years that McDougal faced because he had provided Whitewater investigators "information on a wide range of matters," independent prosecutor Kenneth Starr said.
Before the sentencing, McDougal, 56, told Howard he was placing himself at the mercy of the court.
"I take full and complete responsibility for my crimes and misdeeds...I have no excuses whatsoever to offer to your honour," he said. Along with the jail time, he was fined $10,000.
Starr urged Howard to treat McDougal with leniency because of his cooperation with the Whitewater investigation.

"Mr. McDougal has provided us with information on a wide range of matters, including information heretofore unknown to us," he said. Starr said McDougal also led investigators to information that "independently corroborates substantial portions of (his) accounts."
McDougal, the man at the heart of the Whitewater saga, was found guilty on 18 counts of fraud and conspiracy in a trial last May.
It was one of several legal proceedings arising from the failure of the Madison Savings and Loan Association, which cost taxpayers an estimated $65 million.

Clinton and his wife Hillary entered into a partnership with the McDougals in the Whitewater real estate venture in 1978. Although their investment lost money, questions have arisen about whether funds for the project were siphoned from the savings and loan, which was also a McDougal holding.
